title: C1100B — Battery Connector Reference
introduction:
I use this sheet as the battery connection's address card: identify the connection, match its drawing to the cavity table, then read what that circuit does. The metadata identifies the connector, the harness table associates it with a harness and part reference, and the pin-assignment table supplies the electrical mapping.

In the drawing, a rectangular cable section leads into a broad, rounded terminal end containing the circular cavity label. Match that label to the Cavity column, then read across Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function. Keep the part references in their labeled columns; a terminal part number and a connector base-part field serve different purposes.

This is an identification and wiring-reading guide. It supplies no physical viewing direction, access steps, probing method or electrical test limits. Gauge convention and the Size, Used, Box and Cols codes are not explained here, so I retain them as reference entries without turning them into wire-selection advice. A tidy drawing tells us which connection we're discussing; it cannot certify that the connection is healthy.

edits.why: I match the drawing's cavity label to the pin-assignment table and use the accompanying harness table to confirm the association. The depicted shape helps navigate the reference; it does not establish the physical viewing direction on the vehicle.

Read across the matching cavity row to connect the circuit identifier with its recorded wire attributes, function and terminal reference. A blank Qualifier cell supplies no additional condition, and the unexplained Used code should not be treated as a test result.
